title: Apple Buys AI Audio Editing App Samplab
summary:
Apple acquired AI audio editing app Samplab in June, according to a notice shared today by the European Commission.
Samplab offered a desktop app and plugins for converting audio to MIDI, detecting and editing chords, stem splitting for isolating different parts of a song, and editing notes in polyphonic audio without affecting the timbre of the original.
Apple could fold the company's tools into Logic Pro or GarageBand.
Logic Pro already has Stem Splitter and Chord ID, but polyphonic note editing would be new.
The filing says Apple acquired "certain assets" from Samplab and hired "certain Samplab employees."

title: Louisiana residents are training for jobs at Meta's largest-ever AI data center: 'Why not get in now?'
summary:

summary:

I don't regret moving into AI, but I no longer feel as certain about the decision as I once did.

title: Meta Blames Bot Traffic for No Kings Day Instagram Suspension
summary:
Meta, the owner of Instagram, apologized for disabling an Instagram account run by No Kings Coalition, the organizers of the No Kings Day political rallies held across the country on Saturday.
The timing and duration of the outage were criticized by the No Kings Coalition, which wrote about it on the restored account.

title: Tech Companies Want Workplace Data to Teach AI How Humans Work
summary:
Now they're chasing something even more valuable: data that shows how humans actually work.
That's the focus of Business Insider's new series, The AI Data Grab.
AI firms are offering businesses six- and even seven-figure sums for anonymized Slack messages, emails, presentations, and internal documents.
The goal is to teach AI systems how people solve problems, collaborate, make decisions, and complete long, multi-step tasks.
A third piece, by Rya Jetha, reveals how AI companies pay people to record real-world work, such as cooking dinners and packing warehouses, to teach robots how humans perform everyday physical tasks.

title: Apple’s $250M Siri Settlement Is Taking Claims. Find Out If You Qualify
summary:
The iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing.
Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website.
If you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement.
When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.
According to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval.

title: 75% of Foreign Parts Found in Russian Anti-Jamming Tech From US Firms
summary:
Over two dozen US processors, chips, and other components have been found in Russia's anti-jamming antenna systems, according to Ukraine's military intelligence.
US-headquartered firms produced 28 out of 37 foreign components — or just over three-quarters — listed on Monday, per GUR.
In a statement to Business Insider, a Texas Instruments spokesperson said the company "strongly opposes the use of our chips in Russian military equipment."
Intel, Analog Devices, and Micron did not immediately respond to requests for comment sent outside regular business hours by Business Insider.
